message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Plugin Check on PR
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - trunk

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  plugin-check:
    # Referenced by name from trunk's required status checks: rename both together.
    name: Plugin Check
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Pinned so a new Plugin Check release cannot fail PRs on its own; bump deliberately.
      PLUGIN_CHECK_VERSION: '2.1.0'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      # Check what ships: git archive honors the export-ignore rules in .gitattributes. The
      # directory name becomes the plugin slug.
      - name: Build plugin package
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/action-scheduler
          git archive HEAD | tar -x -C build/action-scheduler

      # The action installs the latest Plugin Check unless one is already installed. It overwrites
      # .wp-env.json, but wp-env merges the override file on top.
      - name: Pin Plugin Check
        run: |
          printf '{ "plugins": [ "https://downloads.wordpress.org/plugin/plugin-check.%s.zip" ] }\\n' "$PLUGIN_CHECK_VERSION" > .wp-env.override.json

      # Existing findings, ignored because they are part of the design or the public API. Each code
      # also suppresses new occurrences, so review before adding to this list. Built here because
      # a YAML block cannot carry a comment per line.
      - name: List ignored codes
        id: ignored
        run: |
          codes=(
            # Exceptions carry plain messages; escaping belongs to whatever displays them.
            WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.ExceptionNotEscaped
            # The data stores query Action Scheduler's own tables.
            WordPress.DB.DirectDatabaseQuery.DirectQuery
            # Queue state must be read fresh, as claims change between requests.
            WordPress.DB.DirectDatabaseQuery.NoCaching
            # SQL is assembled from $wpdb table names and fragments prepared earlier.
            PluginCheck.Security.DirectDB.UnescapedDBParameter
            # The as_*() API and the deprecated wc_*() functions cannot be renamed.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.NonPrefixedFunctionFound
            # The pre_as_* filters are public, and the core hooks are fired deliberately.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.NonPrefixedHooknameFound
            # Actions fire the hooks their schedulers named.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.DynamicHooknameFound
          )
          echo "codes=$(IFS=,; echo "${codes[*]}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Run Plugin Check
        uses: wordpress/plugin-check-action@10857da14b6c2246d15402b3e69f777edcf8c12e # v1.1.9
        with:
          build-dir: build/action-scheduler
          # Report through workflow annotations and the results artifact only.
          repo-token: ''
          # Fail on warnings too.
          strict: true
          ignore-codes: ${{ steps.ignored.outputs.codes }}",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a single required PR check with no matrix, no dependency-install step to cache, and an existing job timeout, so cache, fail-fast, history-timeout, and path-filter optimizations do not fit. The supported optimization is canceling superseded runs (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE): adding a per-PR concurrency group with cancel-in-progress stops stale in-progress checks when a new commit is pushed to the same PR. Preconditions are met: runs are the same workflow on the same branch/PR, a newer revision supersedes older checks, this is not release/deployment work, and the group key uses github.ref so distinct PRs do not share a cancellation group. The required check is preserved because the latest run still completes and reports status. All existing steps and coverage are unchanged.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}

```yaml
name: Plugin Check on PR
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - trunk

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  plugin-check:
    # Referenced by name from trunk's required status checks: rename both together.
    name: Plugin Check
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Pinned so a new Plugin Check release cannot fail PRs on its own; bump deliberately.
      PLUGIN_CHECK_VERSION: '2.1.0'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      # Check what ships: git archive honors the export-ignore rules in .gitattributes. The
      # directory name becomes the plugin slug.
      - name: Build plugin package
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/action-scheduler
          git archive HEAD | tar -x -C build/action-scheduler

      # The action installs the latest Plugin Check unless one is already installed. It overwrites
      # .wp-env.json, but wp-env merges the override file on top.
      - name: Pin Plugin Check
        run: |
          printf '{ \"plugins\": [ \"https://downloads.wordpress.org/plugin/plugin-check.%s.zip\" ] }\\n' "$PLUGIN_CHECK_VERSION" > .wp-env.override.json

      # Existing findings, ignored because they are part of the design or the public API. Each code
      # also suppresses new occurrences, so review before adding to this list. Built here because
      # a YAML block cannot carry a comment per line.
      - name: List ignored codes
        id: ignored
        run: |
          codes=(
            # Exceptions carry plain messages; escaping belongs to whatever displays them.
            WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.ExceptionNotEscaped
            # The data stores query Action Scheduler's own tables.
            WordPress.DB.DirectDatabaseQuery.DirectQuery
            # Queue state must be read fresh, as claims change between requests.
            WordPress.DB.DirectDatabaseQuery.NoCaching
            # SQL is assembled from $wpdb table names and fragments prepared earlier.
            PluginCheck.Security.DirectDB.UnescapedDBParameter
            # The as_*() API and the deprecated wc_*() functions cannot be renamed.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.NonPrefixedFunctionFound
            # The pre_as_* filters are public, and the core hooks are fired deliberately.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.NonPrefixedHooknameFound
            # Actions fire the hooks their schedulers named.
            WordPress.NamingConventions.PrefixAllGlobals.DynamicHooknameFound
          )
          echo "codes=$(IFS=,; echo "${codes[*]}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Run Plugin Check
        uses: wordpress/plugin-check-action@10857da14b6c2246d15402b3e69f777edcf8c12e # v1.1.9
        with:
          build-dir: build/action-scheduler
          # Report through workflow annotations and the results artifact only.
          repo-token: ''
          # Fail on warnings too.
          strict: true
          ignore-codes: ${{ steps.ignored.outputs.codes }}
```
